identity.title: The ALMA Survey of Gas Evolution of PROtoplanetary Disks (AGE-PRO). VI. Comparison of Dust Evolution Models to AGE-PRO Observations

paper_type_evidence.quote: in this study we compare the observational results to dust evolution simulations. Using `DustPy` for the dust evolution, and `RADMC-3D` for the radiative transfer, we ran a large grid of models

targets.name: AGE-PRO sample (30 disks in Ophiuchus, Lupus, Upper Sco)

redshift_or_distance.value: distances from inverse Gaia DR3 parallax

evidence.quote: has allowed for the measurement of the gas mass and size in a sample of 30 disks three different star forming regions (SFRs)
has allowed for the measurement of the gas mass and size in a sample of 30 disks three different star forming regions (SFRs)

question.value: Can dust evolution models (with or without dust traps, viscous gas evolution) reproduce the gas masses, 1.3 mm fluxes, sizes and spectral indices of the AGE-PRO disk sample, and do the data favor dust traps?

evidence.quote: aiming to investigate if any observational trend can favor or exclude the presence of dust traps.
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2021.1.00128.L.
The dual-band setup of the AGE-PRO observations (Band 6 and Band 7 at 1.3-1.05 mm)

angular_resolution.value: average 0.25'' (1.3 mm setup) and 0.8'' (1.05 mm setup) as stated

evidence.quote: The AGE-PRO observations have an average angular resolution of $0.25''$ and $0.8''$ in the 1.3 mm and 1.05 mm setups
normalized to match a sensitivity of $25\,\mu\text{Jy}/\text{beam}$, comparable to AGE-PRO
measured as the inverse of the parallax from Gaia DR3
When comparing against $M_{\rm gas}$ derived from (cite: AGEPRO_V_gasmasses)

what.value: AGE-PRO dust masses and millimeter fluxes

evidence.quote: The dust content of the AGE-PRO disks was calculated directly from the measured millimeter fluxes, and they are presented in (cite: AGEPRO_I_overview)

what.value: AGE-PRO dust disk sizes from visibility modeling

evidence.quote: the AGE-PRO disk sizes were obtained using visibility modeling (cite: AGEPRO_X_dust_disks)

what.value: Stellar masses and ages of the sources

evidence.quote: The full discussion about the estimation of $M_\star$ and age is given in (cite: AGEPRO_I_overview)

simulations_or_models_as_data.value: Grid of DustPy models (M*=0.25-1.0 Msun, Mdisk/M*=0.01/0.05/0.1, rc=15-120 au, Agap=0/1/4, alpha0=1e-4/1e-3, eps0=0.01/0.05), 3 groups of 144 disks saved at 9 ages, with RADMC-3D at 5 ages

evidence.quote: Each of these three groups has 144 disks, which result from choosing the different $M_\star$, $M_{\text{disk}}$, $R_{\rm c}$, and $A_{\rm gap}$.

what.value: AGE-PRO stellar mass and age estimates

evidence.quote: we refer the reader to that work for a detailed description.

what.value: Dust mass opacity and temperature convention (kappa=2.3 (nu/230GHz)^0.4 cm2/g, T=20 K)

evidence.quote: as in (cite: andrews2013). For the temperature, a constant $T=20\,$K is used for consistency with the literature (cite: Ansdell2016).

what.value: Disk radius containing 90% of flux measured as in AGE-PRO

evidence.quote: We calculated the $R_{90\%,cont}$ from the synthetic observations similarly to the AGE-PRO observations (cite: AGEPRO_XI_gas_disk_sizes).

unstated_but_needed: Numerical AGE-PRO observed values (fluxes, radii, gas masses, spectral indices per source) are not tabulated; they must be taken from companion papers
Stellar-mass to model matching of observed sources and any tolerance on how a source is deemed consistent with a model
Exact RADMC-3D inclination/distance settings and flux scaling of images to observed distance
Procedure used to determine total flux and R90 from the model images in the main comparison
Model snapshot data are not released

method.value: 1D DustPy with Lynden-Bell self-similar initial profile, alpha-bump traps, stellar irradiation temperature, run to 10 Myr

evidence.quote: we used the 1D dust evolution code `Dustpy`

key_parameters.value: rin=5 au, rout=500 au, nr=250; mass grid 1e-12 to 3e6 g, nm=134; vfrag=10 m/s; rho_s=1.6 g/cm3

evidence.quote: The standard radial grid of the simulations goes from $r_\textrm{in} = \SI{5}{au}$ to $r_\textrm{out} = \SI{500}{au}$ with $n_r = 250$ logarithmically spaced grid cells.

assumptions.value: Constant alpha in space and time; no back-reaction, photoevaporation or MHD winds; static traps

evidence.quote: our approach does not include mechanisms such as photoevaporation or MHD winds

analysis_steps.goal: Radiative transfer to 1.05 and 1.3 mm images

method.value: RADMC-3D on 30 resampled grain species with Ricci2010 opacities from OpTool, vertical Gaussian hydrostatic dust, two-step Monte Carlo

evidence.quote: First, we ran a Monte Carlo simulation to obtain the dust temperature for every grain species, using $n_\textrm{phot} = 10^7$ photon packages.

key_parameters.value: images with nphot=2e5, isotropic scattering; ages 0.5, 1, 2, 5, 10 Myr; 19440 models

evidence.quote: This implies a total of 19440 radiative transfer models ($5\times3888$).

assumptions.value: Dust composition 10% silicate, 20% carbon, 30% water ice, 40% vacuum

evidence.quote: 10% Silicate (cite: Draine2003), 20% Carbon (cite: Zubko1996), 30% water ice (cite: warren&brandt08), and 40% vacuum.

validation.value: Scattering variations verified to be well below 10% of total flux

evidence.quote: we verified the flux variations were well below 10% of the total flux.

method.value: Compare Mgas, Mpebble vs Mdust, 1.3 mm flux, R90 and spectral index of models to AGE-PRO by age group

evidence.quote: The Ophiuchus sources are compared to our simulations at 0.5 Myr. The Lupus sources are compared to the simulations at 1 Myr and 2 Myr.

key_parameters.value: Mpebble = mass in grains 0.1 mm-10 cm; R90 = radius containing 90% of flux; alpha_mm from B6 and B7 fluxes

evidence.quote: measured by adding the mass content in particles of sizes ranging from $0.1$ mm to $10$ cm

assumptions.value: Optically thin emission, T=20 K for observed dust masses

evidence.quote: it is assumed that the emission is optically thin

validation.value: Synthetic observations with beam convolution and noise tested R90 recovery, robust for disks larger than about three beams

evidence.quote: proves robust for bright disks which are larger than approximately three times the angular resolution of the image
Version 0.5.6 was used for this work.

used_for.value: radiative transfer to produce continuum images

evidence.quote: we used the radiative transfer code `RADMC-3D`
To obtain the dust opacities, we use the code `OpTool`
thus resulting in 3888 different snapshots of the disks evolution.

results_numeric.quantity: Spectral index range in Upper Sco

evidence.quote: A large dispersion in the values of spectral indices is also observed in Upper Sco, ranging between 1.9-3.2
the measured $M_{\rm gas}$ from observations spans $\sim3$ orders of magnitude in Ophiuchus

findings_qualitative.value: Models with weak or strong traps match observed dust masses, fluxes and sizes better than no-trap models

evidence.quote: allows us to exclude disks with no pressure traps as the dominant population in the observations of AGE-PRO

claims.hypothesis: Viscous evolution with constant alpha explains observed gas masses
claims.experiment: Compare no-trap model Mgas to AGE-PRO Mgas
claims.result: Observed range is wider; lowest Ophiuchus masses are 2 orders below models; about half of Lupus and Upper Sco agree
claims.finding: Additional mechanisms (winds, photoevaporation, external effects) are needed

evidence.quote: only about half of the targets in Lupus and Upper Sco are in agreement to the measured $M_{\rm gas}$ of the models

claims.hypothesis: Dust traps are needed to explain dust fluxes and sizes
claims.experiment: Compare 1.3 mm flux and R90 of model grids to AGE-PRO
claims.result: Most disks consistent with weak or strong traps
claims.finding: Traps favored at ages above 1 Myr

evidence.quote: most of the disks in the AGE-PRO sample are consistent with simulations that have either weak or strong dust traps.

claims.experiment: Compare alpha_mm from models and observations
claims.result: Large spread 2-4 only reproduced with traps

evidence.quote: it is only in the presence of dust traps that the spectral index distribution can have a distribution ranging between 2-4 for later ages

limitations_admitted.value: Models were not tailored to individual disks; constant alpha; static traps; simple scattering

evidence.quote: Simulations that are tailored to the properties of each disks will be part of a future publication.

referee_caveats_inferred: Comparison is qualitative, with no statistical fit
Result depends strongly on the Ricci2010 opacity choice
Observations only partly used as data in this paper

data_public_as_stated.value: DustPy publicly available; ALMA data used via companion papers

evidence.quote: `DustPy` is available on [github.com/stammler/DustPy](https://github.com/stammler/DustPy).

reproducibility.estimated_data_volume_inferred: Simulations only; observed values from companion papers (negligible)
reproducibility.score_reason: Model parameters and codes are well specified, but no observational data reduction is involved and the observed values and comparison are from companion papers.
reproducibility.rediscovery_reason: Results are mostly qualitative model-data comparisons; ALMA data reduction not performed here.
